summary: Settled the snapshot question's peer variant by source instead of another execution: the forwarded compaction repeats the same derivation on every receiving node, because each peer's snapshot call compares the requested index against that peer's own decided index — also drifted to 9 in the observed run — and builds the snapshot from that peer's own range, so the peers end in the same loss rather than a different state, with the explicit caveat that their own snapshots were not sampled in the receipt. The rewritten child account keeps the witnessed leader-side loss (snapshot(Some(8), false) returned Ok, compacted index 8, snapshot reachable at index 0 holding zero of the five decided entries, events 0-5), keeps the corrected counter-argument that the equal case is no protection in this state (it lowers the bound from 9 to 8, still above the content of six), and keeps the follower-side and entry-type variants plus the limits (entry-type dependence, unsampled peers, variants argued from the derivation, and the shared-name admission caveat behind the unknown comparison outcomes). The question's discriminator now names only what an execution could still add: the peers' and a directly-called follower's own snapshots and reads after the call. No execution was requested this turn; incomplete are that peer/follower sampling, the trim child's storage-side remainder, the parent drift's bound question, timers and loss triggers, larger clusters, persistence, and any further independent lead.
